subject: geography
title: Drainage Basins and the Hydrological Cycle
welcome_lead: Follow a raindrop from cloud to ocean as it cycles through drainage basins.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: hydrological cycle, drainage basins and storage components.
final_note: You have traced the global plumbing of fresh water. Mass balance underpins all water management.

concepts.def: Closed system circulating water between atmosphere, land and oceans.
Area of land drained by a river and its tributaries, an open subsystem of the hydrological cycle.
Boundary separating one drainage basin from another.
Combined loss of water from soil (evaporation) and vegetation (transpiration).
Lateral movement of water through the soil layer towards streams.

walkthroughs.body_html: The global hydrological cycle is a closed system, exchanging no matter with space. About 97% of water is saline; only ~2.5% is fresh, much of it locked in ice and groundwater. Inputs to a drainage basin include precipitation; outputs include channel discharge, evapotranspiration and deep groundwater loss.

Precipitation may intercept vegetation, run overland (especially on saturated or impermeable surfaces), infiltrate into soil, percolate into rock or reach channels through throughflow and groundwater flow. Lag time between rainfall peak and discharge peak depends on basin shape, soils and land use.

Storage includes ice and snow, groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, and atmospheric water vapour. Residence times vary from days (atmosphere) to thousands of years (deep groundwater). Human activity — dams, irrigation, urbanisation — alters both stores and flows.

options: Watershed
Talweg
Levee
Confluence
Evaporation from soil plus transpiration from plants
Just evaporation from oceans
Just plant transpiration
Rainfall on vegetation

mcqs.q: In a tropical rainforest nutrient cycle, where is most of the nutrient stored?
options: Most nutrients in a rainforest are stored in the soil — that's why plants grow so well.
In the biomass (living plants). Litter is rapidly decomposed by warm humid conditions, and soil is leached — so cycling between biomass and litter dominates.
The ITCZ is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.

mcqs.q: What is the ITCZ and why does it bring rain?
options: Coral bleaching is when boats spill chemicals that whiten the reef.
The ITCZ is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
The ITCZ is a fixed band of permanent storms at the equator.
The Intertropical Convergence Zone is where trade winds from both hemispheres converge near the equator, forcing air to rise, cool and produce heavy convectional rainfall.
Coral bleaching is when boats spill chemicals that whiten the reef.
When stressed (usually by warming), corals expel their symbiotic zooxanthellae (algae that provide colour and food), turning white. They can recover if stress eases, but die if it persists.
Coral bleaching is when coral is killed by sunlight bleaching its colour.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.
